records.description:
The Rural Utilities Service (RUS or the Agency), a Rural Development (RD) agency of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), is soliciting Letters of Interest (LOI) for applications under the Affordable Rural Cooperative (ARC) Program. In addition, the Agency is announcing the eligibility requirements, application process and deadlines, and the criteria that will be used by RUS to assess ARC Applications. The ARC Program is making approximately $175 million in appropriated budget authority for the cost of loan and grant funds available under the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) of 2022. In keeping with the statutory authority for the program, RUS will utilize the ARC funds to assist Eligible Entities to achieve future net reductions consistent with Section 22004 of the IRA through the deployment of advanced, efficient transmission infrastructure and nuclear power supply. Available funds will be allocated for each purpose while advancing the long-term resiliency, reliability, and affordability of rural electric systems. All Eligible Entities are responsible for any expenses incurred in developing their LOIs and ARC Applications.


This funding notice advances the statutory purpose of achieving the greatest reductions as provided in Section 22004 of the IRA associated with rural electric systems by increasing the amount of emission-free nuclear power and increasing the efficiency of the transmission grid within such systems. These new sources of cooperative power supply and enhanced transmission efficiency will result in reduced future demand for other sources of power.


Cost Sharing or Matching:

For Project and System loans, RUS will finance up to 75 percent of the total capitalized cost of the Project in the loan component of a Project and/or System Award. The Awardee will be required to initially provide and maintain for the term of the Project and/or System Award at least 25 percent of the Project’s total capitalized cost in the form of cash or an equity investment.


As noted in Section 2.0 of the NOFO, the Agency may where Financially Feasible allow an Awardee to utilize the grant component of the Award and/or any applicable tax credit that it expects to receive (including credit amounts expected to be received through Elective Pay elections under section 6417 of the Internal Revenue Code) toward the 25 percent equity requirement for a Project Award. Such financial equity may not come from the proceeds of any loan from any creditor, including insiders of the Awardee.

post.description:
Search Grants.gov funding opportunities by keyword, agency, status, eligibility, funding category, assistance listing and posted-date window; one page of summary records (or full records with expand).

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 provider_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

agency_ids.description: Grants.gov agency codes (e.g. HHS-NIH11, NSF, USDA-RUS). Department-level codes without a hyphen (e.g. HHS, DOD) are expanded to all sub-agencies using one extra facet request. Use `facets` to list codes.

cursor.description: next_cursor from a previous response with the same filters. Cursors from a different filter set, malformed cursors, or cursors beyond depth 10000 are rejected with invalid_input.

eligibilities.description: Two-digit Grants.gov applicant eligibility codes, e.g. 00 State governments, 01 County governments, 02 City or township governments, 04 Special district governments, 05 Independent school districts, 06 Public and State controlled institutions of higher education, 07 Native American tribal governments (Federally recognized), 08 Public housing authorities/Indian housing authorities, 11 Native American tribal organizations (other than Federally recognized), 12 Nonprofits having a 501(c)(3) status, 13 Nonprofits without 501(c)(3), 20 Private institutions of higher education, 21 Individuals, 22 For profit organizations other than small businesses, 23 Small businesses, 25 Others, 99 Unrestricted. Any code matches (OR).

expand.description: Fetch the full detail record for every hit (one extra upstream request each; requires page_size <= 20).

funding_categories.description: Grants.gov funding activity category codes, e.g. AG Agriculture, AR Arts, BC Business and Commerce, CD Community Development, CP Consumer Protection, DPR Disaster Prevention and Relief, ED Education, ELT Employment/Labor/Training, EN Energy, ENV Environment, FN Food and Nutrition, HL Health, HO Housing, HU Humanities, ISS Income Security and Social Services, IS Information and Statistics, LJL Law/Justice/Legal Services, NR Natural Resources, RA Recovery Act, RD Regional Development, ST Science and Technology, T Transportation, O Other. Any code matches (OR). Use `facets` for the live list.

funding_instruments.description: G Grant, CA Cooperative Agreement, PC Procurement Contract, O Other.

opportunity_number.description: Exact-ish funding opportunity number filter (source oppNum).

page_size.description:
page_size

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 100; default 20.

published_from.description: Earliest posted date (inclusive), YYYY-MM-DD. The source has no date filter, so a window forces posted_desc sort and scans up to 5 upstream pages (500 records) per call, resuming via next_cursor. Pattern: ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$.

published_to.description: Latest posted date (inclusive), YYYY-MM-DD. Must not be earlier than published_from. Pattern: ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$.

query.description:
Keyword(s) matched by Grants.gov full-text search over title, number, description and agency. Separate words are matched with OR (`community solar` returns every notice mentioning either word); wrap a multi-word concept in double quotes (`"community solar"`) for an exact-phrase match. A multi-term query adds a warning saying so. Empty = browse.

Provider reference: default "".

sort.description:
Ordering. A publication-date window requires posted_desc.

Provider reference: allowed values ["relevance", "posted_desc", "posted_asc", "close_asc", "close_desc"]; default "posted_desc".

statuses.description: Normalized status. posted = open for applications (source `posted`); forecast = planned, not yet open (source `forecasted`); closed = deadline passed, still listed (source `closed`); archived = removed from the public search after its archive date (source `archived`). Default posted+forecast; add closed/archived explicitly.
